sections.text: Lord Shri Krishna said: This imperishable philosophy I taught to Viwaswana, the founder of the Sun dynasty, Viwaswana gave it to Manu the lawgiver, and Manu to King Ikshwaku!
The Divine Kings knew it, for it was their tradition. Then, after a long time, at last it was forgotten.
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः।
It is the same ancient Path that I have now revealed to thee, since thou art My devotee and My friend. It is the supreme Secret.

We had been discussing chapter four, Gnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga -- Yoga of Renouncing Karma in Knowledge. We have completed discussion on chapter three, Karma Yoga. In Karma Yoga we have seen how to act in this world so that we are not bound by our actions.
But our goal actually in life is to become actionless, to retire from my activity. So if somebody says, Why, Rajan, you are working so hard? -- well, I am working hard to become actionless in my retirement. And how do I want to achieve that? If I can become financially independent so that I dont depend on the outside income.
As long as Im dependent on outside income, I have to keep working. I need to generate income from outside sources, so Im continuing to work. The harder I work, obviously the more conflicts I create and more situation which makes me unhappy.
More I think Im controlling the situation. The situation controls me. So what I want to do is to create a situation where I dont have to work with the outside world for my well being.
Thats what we call retirement. So thats why we have this 401k and IRA and all of that. That will make me independent.
Once Im financially independent and I dont depend on my outside income, then I can do what I want. Every year I took a cruise, and I realized that most of the population of the cruise is above 55 -- 80% of the people were senior citizens. So all the programs were geared towards senior citizens.
So I was actually pitying all the young people who were there like in minority. I want to do what I want to do. So the goal is always to be actionless, that I dont want to interact with this world.
In the last chapter we learned exactly the same thing. For all these activities it says Yahatu Atmaratiyeva: everyone has a duty to act in this world according to their own dharma, according to the roles they are playing. It comes with all the Niyata Karma, all these ordained duties.
So you have to continue doing your duties. But there is Only one exception. One who is atmaratihi who is reveling in himself.
Hes not dependent on anything or anybody outside to be happy. Atmatruptastamaanava who is self content. If Im reveling in myself, Im self content.
Atmani evacha santushtaha tasya kariyam na vidyaday -- the only time you have no duty to act, to do any work or any action, is when you meet this condition. Atmaratehe -- full of yourself. Not a right way to put it, but you get the idea.
So you have no real need to depend on the outside world. Once you are not depending on the outside world, there is no question of having a conflict with it. Its only when we are dependent on them that we have conflict.
I am dependent on my employees. My employees are dependent on me. We constantly have conflict. You are not coming on time.
You didnt do what I thought you were going to be doing. He feels the same way: Rajan, you are not doing what I thought you were going to do for me. Because we are dependent on each other. If I am not dependent on them, there is no conflict. We have a project at Dominion and its really going nowhere because we are updating the auditorium.
The CEO of the company will be at the first meeting there on the 23rd. And the project is supposed to be complete end of March. It is not completed now.
We dont know whether its going to complete on the 23rd. So theyre working overtime hours because the CEO is going to be there, they call me up, they call everybody. Obviously we blame everybody else who contracted into this. Why did you specify this, Rajan? They say, Something which comes from Japan, all this good stuff.
So I asked the guys, Did you always have this problem? The guy whos in charge at Dominion said, The only time I dont have a problem is when I dont depend on anybody. When I do work myself, thats fine. But otherwise, I have to depend on the contractor.
I have to depend on you. We all know for sure: when I dont have to depend on other people, then Im free. He has no employees to worry about. His structural engineer was a one man firm and did very well, because hes not dependent on his employees.
He knows what he can do, what he cannot do, and he can promise accordingly. In my case, I have to depend on 15 other people when I promise what theyre going to do. So in our life we have figured out that the only way to be free is not to be dependent on anybody.
At the same token, my happiness right now is mortgaged to this world outside. They determine whether I can be happy or not. So Bhagawan said that the goal of life is to become actionless.
Ill become actionless when Im not dependent on others for my happiness. So we learn that Yahatu Atmaratihiva, one who is reveling in himself, atmatrupta satisfied by his own self, atmaniyevacha Santustah is content by himself. Then he does not have to do anything.
But the same token, I have to continue to work in this world. So I need to understand what is the way I can stop acting. And this chapter, the title says Gnana Karma Sannyasa.
When the knowledge occurs -- what is happiness? What is it that Im seeking? -- then all actions I can renounce. So now we are further taking our discussion on actions to next level. We understood that I need to act in a manner that Im not attached to the actions.
And also I should be acting in a way that it is good for everyone, that is for the greater good. Then I will not be bound by my actions. But how do I reach to that point? I need to have the knowledge.
My actions without knowledge obviously are not producing the result which I need to produce. So the next level of discussion in the actions is now how do you achieve that state where I have the knowledge? So the chapter titled Gnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga Bhagawan doesnt even wait for Arjuna to ask any question. He comes out and gives him his version of what were going to do next.
Sri Bhagavanu Vacha Imam Vivasvate Yogam proktavan Aham Avyam Vivasvaan Manavai Praha Manohu Isvakave Abravit said, Im now going to teach you the yoga which is imperishable. That knowledge has never become outdated. We used to learn something probably in last century about driving a horse buggy.
In this century we are learning how to drive car. It will become invalid pretty soon if these guys are all successful. We used to put a lot of emphasis on handwriting, at least architecture.
Our whole life in the architecture school was how nicely I can write. Its called architectural script. We spent all our life to perfect our handwriting.
Nobody writes anymore. You cant differentiate my drawing from anybody else. We used to take great pride in that.
Even if there is work left and there is not enough time, and somebody says, Can I help you, Rajan? -- I want to make sure that nobody elses handwriting is on my drawing. Because once somebody says, Oh, thats Rajans drawing, I dont want somebody elses handwriting on it. But now all drawings look the same, no matter where they come from, because its all computer.
So the skills which we were learning, which was so dear to us is no more valid. But one said this yoga is not like that, its universal. It was always valid in the past, its valid now and it will be valid forever.
Ivam Vivasvate Yogam Proktava vyam I taught this yoga to Vivaswan and then Vivaswan Manavai Prah Vivaswan then taught in turn to the Manu. The Manu in dint taught to Manu Isva kavet. He is now making sure that you understand that this is not something I just made up suddenly.
This is an imperishable yoga. This knowledge is imperishable. Its applicable at any given age.
So it starts with that. This knowledge is so ancient. It starts with the beginning of this creation.
In our world, the creation started with Sun. We at least know from our high school science that this earth came out of Sun. And then obviously all the development in the earth is because of that solar energy.
So our source at our level is Sun. We dont have to go any further than that. So he said, even when the sun was created, this knowledge was there.
So Vivaswani -- for the first time, Krishna comes out as I am the Lord. In this conversation, the Creator, the knowledge giver, is saying this knowledge was always available from the beginning of this creation. So I gave it to the first created entity, the Sun. That Sun gave it to his son, which is Manu.
From our puranic point of view, Viva Swan was the original entity. Manu was his son, and then the whole progeny starts and we end up here. In this class I taught to Lord sun who is the originator of our world.
Then he in turn taught to his sons. Obviously we always pass on our knowledge from us to our children. Thats why we start teaching the little kids.
And yesterday we were in the park and Medha always like to swing. The only way to stop her is say were going to count one to hundred. So in 100 you have to come down.
Thats okay, we start 1, 2. And she said no, were going to count in Spanish. So she starts -- uno, dwe.
Okay, after that what? Meda, after that what? Because she has to tell us now. She knows because of Dora the Explorer. So we teach our children what we know.
So Bhagavan said that Lords son taught to his sons what he knew, this imperishable yoga. Then Manu in turn taught to his son. So Ishvaku, Ishwaku, we all know from Ramayana is the ancestor of Rama of the Sun Dynasty.
Sun Dynasty came from this lineage, whether we like this historically or not. But thats how the Puranas describe our lineage. The point here is very simple: right from the beginning of our ancestry, this knowledge was available to people.
And those people passed it on from one generation to another through the leaders of the society. The leaders obviously in those days were kings. They were the people who were leading the society.
So if you read historically, Manu led these people from wherever they were to land which was safer and more fertile. Actually, Professor Bargha said that Noah is the same as Manu, because in Sanskrit Manu is Manu-hu. The people in the Arabic world only kept Nu. They dropped the Ma, and then Nu in the western world became Noah. So if you read the story of Noahs Ark, it is very similar to what we have in our Puranas about the Great Flood.
So we know that theres some connection somewhere where some ancestor left some land which was not very conducive and was flooding all the time, and led his people to somewhere safer. So he led his people to this. So hes our ancestor Manu Adi Manu.
And whether he was the first human being is left to your imagination. We know for sure that he was the first Aryan king in this lineage of the Aryan kings who ruled Arya worth for ages. So he said the first person to know this knowledge in this lineage, Manu.
Manu in turn will give it to his sons. He came to Ishwaku who was the ancient king of Solar dynasty.

These opening verses of Chapter 4 reveal something profound: the wisdom Krishna shares with Arjuna is not new but imperishable (avyayam), passed from teacher to student since the beginning of creation. This knowledge was given first to Vivaswan (the Sun), then to Manu, then to Ikshvaku, forming an unbroken chain of transmission. Consider that you too are part of this lineage of seekers. The fact that this teaching has survived millennia, passed through royal sages and philosopher-kings, suggests it addresses something fundamental about human existence that transcends time and culture.
Krishna reveals this supreme secret to Arjuna because he is both a devotee (bhakta) and a friend (sakha). This teaches us that spiritual knowledge is not merely intellectual but relational. Ask yourself today: Who are my spiritual teachers, formal or informal? Am I approaching this wisdom with the humility of a student and the openness of a friend? What ancient wisdom traditions have been passed to me through my own family, culture, or chosen path?
As a daily exercise, identify one piece of timeless wisdom you received from a parent, grandparent, or mentor. Reflect on how this imperishable knowledge has helped guide your actions. Consider how you might pass on such wisdom to others, becoming a link in the chain yourself. The goal of this teaching is to become actionless at the core, not dependent on the outside world for happiness, but reveling in your own Self (atmaratih).
